value.body: The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and the State Pollution Control Boards / Committees monitor air, water and noise pollution, run testing labs, and issue consents to industries. They recruit scientific and technical staff such as scientists, environmental engineers, and junior / senior scientific and lab assistants.

items.label: Who hires
items.value: CPCB and each State Pollution Control Board or Committee

items.label: Typical posts
items.value: Scientist, Environmental Engineer, Scientific Assistant, Lab Assistant

items.label: Qualification
items.value: Science degree (often a master's) in Environmental Science, Chemistry or related subjects

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Watch the CPCB and your state board's recruitment notices; some states recruit through the state PSC or staff selection board. Selection is usually a written test, sometimes with an interview or skill test. Many scientist posts ask for a master's degree; assistant posts often accept a B.Sc.

value.title: At a glance
items: Recruitment is irregular and differs from state to state.
Work includes sampling, lab analysis, industry inspections and consent processing.
Contract and project posts also appear, alongside regular posts.
